newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SOCCER-FIFA URGE SUSPENSION OF TOP AUSTRALIAN CLUB.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIFA URGE SUSPENSION OF TOP AUSTRALIAN CLUB.

text.p: FIFA has urged Soccer Australia to suspend top club Sydney United for taking the domestic governing body to court in a bid to avoid possible axing from the national league because of crowd trouble.
In a letter released by Soccer Australia on Friday, the sport's world body said United should be barred from competition until they drop their current court case.
In a message released on Friday by Soccer Australia, FIFA said: "We herewith urge you (SA) to immediately suspend club Sydney United until they withdraw their complaint in the Supreme Court."
By winning an injunction last week, United prevented Soccer Australia from taking disciplinary action over crowd violence at a national league match in May.
Soccer Australia reported United's action to FIFA as a breach of its international statutes banning clubs from taking a national association to court.
United officials resorted to the courts after an internal SA inquiry held the club responsible for their fans' behaviour.
Before the inquiry began, SA chairman David Hill said an adverse finding could lead to Sydney United's expulsion from the national league.
FIFA also directed SA to take any disciplinary action it feels appropriate against the club for the original crowd trouble and the subsequent decision to take legal action.

"We consider this as a very serious case and your club Sydney United must be informed of the consequences for not complying with the statutes and regulations of the Australia Soccer and FIFA," the message from FIFA said.
